sentences.text:

 THIS M.F.A. AND M.F.A. CROB.
COMING ON FOR FINAL HEARING, THIS DAY, K.S.MUDAGAL J., DELIVERED THE FOLLOWING:
JUDGMENT Heard both side.
2. This appeal arises out of the award dated 18.04.2012 in LAC No.98/2011 passed by Principal Senior Civil Judge, Hassan.
Challenging the said award respondent No.1 has filed cross-objection in MFA CROB.No.47/2015.

3. Five guntas of land in Sy.No.43/2D2 of Chikkahonenahalli Village of Hassan Taluk, along with many other lands were acquired for the purpose of construction of Veterinary Medical College coming under the Karnataka Veterinary, Animal and Fisheries Sciences University, Bidar.

entities.text: Karnataka Veterinary, Animal and Fisheries Sciences University, Bidar
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: Preliminary notification was issued on 21.05.2007.
Final notification was issued on 05.10.2007.
4. Respondent No.2 passed the award on 20.10.2009.

On the requisition of respondent No.1 for enhancement of compensation, the matter was referred to the Principal Senior NC:
2023:KHC:21537-DB Civil Judge, Hassan under Section 18(1) of the Land Acquisition Act.

The same was registered in LAC No.98/2011.
5.
Admittedly the beneficiary of the acquisition was the Chancellor, Karnataka Veterinary, Animal and Fisheries Sciences University, Bidar.

entities.text: Karnataka Veterinary, Animal and Fisheries Sciences University, Bidar
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: That is evident from the General/Consent award dated 20.10.2009 produced by respondent No.1/Cross- objector by way of additional evidence.

However,
in the reference petition, the Dean of the Veterinary Medical College, Hassan was shown as beneficiary.

Accordingly in LAC No.98/2011 he was impleaded as respondent No.2.
6.
The impugned award shows that District Government Pleader accepted the notice for respondent No.2, though he was not authorized to do so.
Without any intimation to the appellant, he cross examined the claimant.
The evidence of respondent/appellant was taken as nil.
According to the appellant/beneficiary, they had no notice of the proceedings in LAC No.98/2011 at all.
The reference Court by the impugned award allowed the reference petition awarding compensation of Rs.75/- per Sq.ft.

Sri K.N Phanindra, learned Senior Counsel appearing for Smt. Vaishali Hegde, learned counsel on The Veterinary Medical College vs Smt Puttalaxmamma on 21 June, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/108897913/
3 record for the appellant submits that the impugned award is in violation of principles of natural justice and the appellant had no notice of the proceeding at all.
8.

entities.text: Veterinary Medical College vs Smt Puttalaxmamma
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Per contra Sri B.M Mohan Kumar, learned Counsel for respondent No.1/claimant submits that in the connected matter under General/Consent award, compensation was awarded at the same rate and that was not challenged by the appellant.
9. Shri
. K.N.Phanindra
, learned Senior counsel submits that some of those awards are challenged and such awards came to the notice of the appellant only when they received the notice in execution petition.
The fact remains that the beneficiary of acquisition was not impleaded in the reference petition as party and whoever was impleaded was not represented by authorized persons.

10. In the similar circumstance, the Coordinate Bench of this Court in MFA No.6419/2015 (LAC) by the order dated 04.06.2021 set aside the impugned award and remanded the NC:
2023:KHC:21537-DB matter to the Reference Court on the same ground.
The same principle applies here also.
The matter is already pending since more than a decade.
The matter shall not be prolonged before the Reference Court after remand.
Therefore matter can be remanded for disposal in a time bound manner.

Hence the following:
ORDER
The appeal and Cross-objection are allowed.
(i) The impugned judgment and award dated 18.04.2012 in LAC No.98/2011 on the file of the Principal Senior Civil Judge, Hassan is hereby set aside.
(ii) The matter is remanded to the Reference Court for fresh consideration after affording reasonable opportunity to both parties.
(iii) The parties shall appear before the Reference Court on 17.07.2023 without any further notice.
(iv) Reference Court shall then afford reasonable opportunities to both the parties and dispose of the matter as expeditiously as possible, at any rate, within six months from 17.07.2023.
NC: 2023:KHC:21537-DB (v) Registry shall transmit the TCRs and amount in deposit to the Reference Court forth with and communicate the copy of this order to the Reference Court.
(vi) Registry shall refund the Court fee paid by the parties to them.

Pending IAs stood disposed of accordingly.
Sd/-
JUDGE Sd/-
